# The Agent's Core, Safety and Provider Changes (Plan 5A) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the plain Kotlin core of Kestrel's agent (sub-project 5): the module `:core:screen-model` with the snapshot model and its title and signature rules, the provider changes for the agent's requests (per-task context, cache breakpoints, the tool-choice flag), the safety check with its categories, modes, floor, allowance, links, emergency guard, redaction, vault, agent-free apps, test mode's self-chats and confirmations, and `:core:agent`'s ports, observation, tools, conversation, loop, limits, memory and routines, all tested on the JVM with a scripted model.

**Architecture:** `:core:screen-model` holds the plain Kotlin snapshot model that `:core:screen` used to hold, so that the plain modules `:core:safety` and `:core:agent` can read snapshots (design D1, review note R1). `:core:safety` is a set of pure functions over a proposal, a fresh snapshot, the task's state and the settings (D13 to D18). `:core:agent` reaches the rest of Kestrel only through its ports (`ScreenPort`, `EyesPort`, `DataPort`, `OwnerPort`, `ModelPort`, `AppsPort`, `MemoryStore`, `TaskLog`, `AgentClock`), so the whole loop runs in JVM tests with `ScriptedModel` and the fakes of its test fixtures; plans 5B and 5C implement the ports in `:app`, `:core:datatools` and `:core:perception`, whose empty modules this plan creates with the anchors that they insert below.

**Tech Stack:** Kotlin 2.4.21, kotlinx.serialization 1.13.0, kotlinx.coroutines 1.11.0, JUnit 4, OkHttp 5.5.1's `mockwebserver3` for `:core:providers`' tests, Gradle's `java-test-fixtures` plugin, PowerShell 7.3 for `scripts\hook.ps1`'s anchor and Pester 6.2.0 for `scripts\test-scripts.ps1`.

## Global Constraints

- Package and application ID `dev.kestrel`; licence GPL-3.0-or-later. One new dependency ships in the release app: `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android:1.28.0` (MIT) as an `implementation` of `:core:perception`, pinned by the audit and by Gradle's verification metadata (plan 5C). Nothing else new ships; `java-test-fixtures` adds no dependency, and the test fixtures use only Kotlin, coroutines and kotlinx.serialization, because the audit checks the debug runtime classpath (review C M13). No Python, Pillow, piexif or exiftool in any script.
- `minSdk 33`, `targetSdk 37`, `compileSdk 37`. Every call that the A71 (API 33) lacks (`takeScreenshotOfWindow`, `READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED`, `getTooltipText` is API 28 and fine) has a check of the API level.
- No dependency-injection framework; `AppGraph` wires by hand. `:core:agent` and `:core:safety` stay plain Kotlin. Every new coroutine scope (the task runner, the agent's loop, the memory and routine stores, the notification listener, the OCR engine) reports its failures through `graph.errors`, by class only (D32 item 48).
- All network traffic goes through `NetworkGateway`; no new module names a type or calls a method that the audit flags, `audit/rules.txt` gets no new network exception, and `Geocoder`, the network and fused location providers and Google's location client are never used.
- No request to any provider's API outside the owner's second sitting (D30): not in a plan's step, a test or a script; every agent test uses the scripted model, and a task given through H1 refuses to run without it unless a live sitting is open (D28).
- Every device check is automated (the owner's rule of 2026-11-20): a script gives each task or command as text through a debug hook and checks the result on the device; speech is checked with generated clips through the PC's speakers; the owner is asked only for sign-ins and links, one real touch and answers only he can give, in one short step at the start of a sitting (D30); the scripts unlock the A71 with the test PIN through plan 4D's unlock function (Q6; review C3 nit 1). Checks match a result to the task number of the text that they sent, never to the newest task. The OCR files and the Python reference are fetched once by plan 5C's writer from ModelScope, Hugging Face and GitHub, which are not providers' APIs.
- Never log, print or put into a test's output the owner's words, screen text, a notification, an SMS, an e-mail, a contact, a prompt, a reply, a tool's arguments, a screenshot, a vault value, the A71's PIN, a token or a key; `toString` of anything that carries them prints only kinds, counts or lengths (D25). Failures are logged by their classes and stack frames only. Screenshots stay in memory.
- Device tests never touch the owner's contacts, calendar, messages, photos, profiles or spending; they use test-only data and remove it, also after a failure.
- Test only on kestrel-api37 (check `adb -s <serial> emu avd name` in the same command as each device command); never on the S23+ or the AVD `zoran`; the A71 only in the two sittings (D30). The main session owns `.superpowers/sdd/emulator.lock` (process rule 9); subagents never create, wait for or delete it. Only one Gradle build at a time. Gradle only through `scripts\gradle.ps1`, stopped with `--stop` at the end of each task; device tests only through `scripts\connected-test.ps1` (with `-Pandroid.injected.androidTest.leaveApksInstalledAfterRun=true`) or the scripts that a plan names; installs only through `scripts\install.ps1`.
- No device test, script or session step ever places a call to an emergency number or answers "yes, call" (process rule 10); test mode blocks every agent call, and the agent hands every call over in every mode (D13). The fixtures use only fictional addresses and the fictional number of D28.
- Scripts run on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, or declare `#Requires -Version 7.3` as `hook.ps1` does; `scripts\test-scripts.ps1` passes after every script change.
- The repository uses LF line endings.
- The plan files are named with the day they are written (`Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd`): this plan is `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-agent-5a-core-safety-providers.md`; plans 5B and 5C follow the design's names. A plan is frozen once committed; a later difference goes into `.superpowers/sdd/progress.md`.

D-numbers refer to the design `.superpowers/sdd/plan-5-design.md`. Code comments call it "design D… of sub-project 5", as the code of sub-project 4 names its design. Plan 5A has no device step: every test runs on the JVM, and every agent test uses the scripted model.

## Before you start

- The code is `origin/main` after plan 4D and its final fixes, or later commits of this plan. Plan 4D changes files that this plan changes too (`app/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/commands/CallCommands.kt`, `app/src/debug/kotlin/dev/kestrel/app/debug/TestHooks.kt`, `scripts/hook.ps1`, `README.md` and the spec); this plan was written against plan 4D's text of them and replaces only the texts that it quotes. The counts at the start of this plan are those at the end of plan 4D. The controller gives their values in each task's brief: `:app` JVM tests A₀ (with the debug-only JVM tests of `app/src/testDebug`, which `:app:testDebugUnitTest` runs too), `:core:commands` C₀, `:core:providers` P₀, `:core:safety` F₀ and `:core:screen` S₀; `:core:screen-model` and `:core:agent` do not exist yet. Each task gives its counts as "N + k", where N is the count before the task; before each task, compare the counts with the ones that the earlier tasks left. If a count differs, stop and ask the controller.
- Before each task, check that every text that the task replaces exists, and exists once, in its file. If a text is missing, stop and ask the controller.
- Before each task, run `git status --short`. If a file that the task changes (its **Files** list) already shows changes that are not the task's own, stop and ask the controller, because the task's `git add` would commit them too.
- Run Gradle only through `scripts\gradle.ps1`, and stop it with `scripts\gradle.ps1 --stop` at the end of each task. Only one Gradle build may run on this computer at a time (process rule 8b); if another agent's build runs, wait for it to end.
- No step of this plan uses a device, the emulator lock, a provider's API or the network beyond Gradle's own dependency cache.
- Every commit message ends with the line `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Not in this plan

- Plan 5B (the data tools, the screen's safety, the Orchestrator, the app and the fixtures): `:core:datatools`' code (the contacts moved from `:app`, `find_contact`, media, calendar, alarms, SMS, the call log, location, navigation, browsers, the settings pages' intents, the notification listener); `:core:screen`'s `OwnActions`, `OwnerSignal`, `PressPolicy`, `UNCERTAIN`, `setText`'s `expected`, `openUri`'s `packageName` and `browsable`, `openIntent`, the card's arming delay, and the reads of `tooltip` and `scrollAxis` from Android's nodes; the Orchestrator's task phases, questions, pause and "Kestrel, continue"; `:app`'s `AgentRunner`, `AppScreenPort`, `AppOwnerPort`, `AppModelPort`, `SettingsMemoryStore`, `LogTaskLog`, `AgentTexts`, `PermissionActivity`, the Safety and Memory pages, the checklist's two steps; `:testapp`'s fixtures (the messenger whose chat header has the view ID `chat_title`, Task 1's `ScreenTitles` entry), the debug hooks below the 5B anchors, `scripts\task-check.ps1`; the emulator's entries of `systemui-parts.json` and `ScreenTitles`; and its part of the spec (D31's 5B list).
- Plan 5C (looking closer, speech checks and the sittings): `:core:perception`'s OCR, `ScreenCapture`, `hideAllForCapture`, `showBadges`, the `EyesPort` implementation, the screenshot question, the OCR model files, the speech checks, `scripts\a71-agent.ps1`, the two sittings and their part of the spec (D31's 5C list).

## Changes to the design that this plan makes

- `port.MemoryStore` is created by Task 10 with the facts and the screenshot approvals, which `remember`, `forget` and `look_closer` need from the loop's first version; Task 13 adds route notes and found contacts, and Task 14 routines and signatures.
- `ScreenPort` gets `resolve(intent: IntentSpec): String?`, which `LinkCheck` (D32 item 12), `open_settings`' fallback list and Firefox's "is it installed" need, and `waitForFront` gets the front package before the action, for the case without a known package (D11).
- `OwnerPort` gets `gate(): Gate`, the agent's gate before a model call, an action and a question while a task is paused (D2).
- `SafetyCheck` has `assess` (which returns the category, its sources and the decisions before and after test mode, for the activity log's `SAFETY` entry, D25 and D27) beside `decide`, and `afterAction`, which keeps the share flow, the protected trail and the typed texts, because a pure check cannot remember them itself.
- `ScreenTree` (in `:core:screen-model`) holds the plain questions about a snapshot's tree that both the safety check and the agent ask (the front window, ancestors, scrollable and vertical lists, toolbars), and `Region` the 3×3 grid of D6 and D8.
- `ConfirmationBuilder` is created in Task 3 with the forms that need no recipient (deleting, typing, the allowance's question) and gets the recipient forms in Task 5, because `SafetyCheck`'s `Confirm` needs a confirmation from Task 3 on.
- `ScreenTitles` gets only Telegram's header rule (r63: no view IDs) and the `:testapp` messenger's `chat_title`; the entries of WhatsApp, Gmail, Google Messages, Samsung Messages and Settings come from the recorded trees (5B and the controller), because no source names their header IDs.
- `SelfChats.ACTIVE` is empty in this plan: by D18's one rule, an app's self-chat rule is active only after a reviewed fix pins it from a real tree, so test mode blocks every send until then, except to a fixture that `selfChatAliases` maps.
- Review 4's I7 splits the outline's Task 10 in two: Task 10 is the loop with the screen actions, the safety check, confirmations, hand-overs and the report, and Task 11 adds the data tools, links, settings pages, `look_closer` and the share flow's one yes. So plan 5A has 15 tasks, and the outline's Tasks 11 to 14 are Tasks 12 to 15 here.
- `TaskReport` and `EndReason` are created by Task 10 with the loop, not with the limits (Task 12), because `Agent.run` hands a report on every path from its first version (D32 item 4); Task 12 adds the limits and the completion check to the loop. `Ledger` comes with them, because a cancelled task's report needs it.
- `EndReason` gets four values beside D7's list: `TEST_MODE` (D18's block ends the task), `CONTEXT_TOO_SMALL` (D32 item 10's sentence), `MODEL_UNUSABLE` (D32 items 36 and 37 for the lightweight model) and `KESTREL_ERROR` (an unexpected failure inside the agent, which still reports once and is rethrown for `graph.errors`). `TaskCancellation(reason)` lets `:app` cancel a task's job with `CANCELLED` or `PAUSED_TOO_LONG`.
- `look_closer`'s agent side (D20's three steps, the masks and the screenshot question) is in Task 11's `LookCloser`, because no task of the outline names it and the ports that it needs exist from Task 6.
- The relabelled earlier observation is Task 6's `Observation.earlier()`; the conversation's tail starts at the step that holds the second-newest observation, and a data tool's lines shrink to their summary as observations do.
- When the two roles name the same model, a switch moves the task to the versatile role anyway (with its reasoning level), so that the "keep trying?" question can come; D7's "only resets the counts" would otherwise switch forever.
- The recent-apps and home screens are refused by the `EyesPort` implementation (plan 5C), which can read `config_recentsComponentName`; the agent refuses agent-free apps and Play services itself.
- D14's "Kestrel opens Cc and Bcc when they are collapsed" is the loop's `EmailCopies` (Task 10), by the controller's decision: before it asks about a send, the loop taps, once per task and only after the safety check lets it run as reading, the one element of an e-mail app's front window (Gmail now; plan 5B adds the packages that it records) whose name is made of Cc and Bcc words, when the window shows a To field and no Cc or Bcc field (review 4 I2).
- A refused versatile model ends a task that would switch to it as `STUCK`; D32 item 36 could also be read as "go on with the lightweight model", but a task that needs the switch is stuck on that model already (review 5 N6).
- D24's second sign of a crash, the app gone from the front without an action of Kestrel's, is not detected, because an action that opens a link or a share sheet changes the front app in the same way; the model sees the new screen (review 4 m6).
- The offer to save a routine after the second run with the same signature is asked by `:app` after it has spoken the report (`TaskReport.offerRoutine`), not by the agent before the report (review 5 M10).
- The task message redacts the owner's words (and a routine's note) on their own and adds Kestrel's date and allowance lines after, because one pass over the whole message read the year beside "code" in "Read me the code" as a one-time code.
- Plans 5B and 5C get anchors in `scripts/hook.ps1` beside the help text: below `# sub-project 5B: agent hook names` and `# sub-project 5C: live hook names` in the `ValidateSet` of `$Command`, below `# sub-project 5B: agent parameters` and `# sub-project 5C: live parameters` in `param(...)`, and below `# sub-project 5B: agent extras` and `# sub-project 5C: live extras` after the last extra; each name or parameter line that they add ends with a comma, so that the two plans never change the same lines (review 1 I1).
- `Signature.sameScreen` compares the package, the window's kind and the parts, not the window's ID, because Android gives every window instance a new ID, also the same screen after its app restarted, and a routine recorded in an earlier session could otherwise never replay (D6, D23; review 1 I2). The signature's regions, and the observation's, are measured above the keyboard (`ScreenTree.visibleArea`), so that the keyboard opening or closing is never another screen (D6; review 3 I3).
- In Copilot's explicit cache mode the system prompt gets a breakpoint too, and a Chat Completions route with Anthropic's `cache_control` sends the system prompt and the context as two marked blocks of its one system message, so that every task reads the tools and the system prompt from the cache (the controller's decision on review 1 M3).
- A share flow's question and test mode read the rows, the chat or the dialog that the screen shows at the moment of the send, never the rows that the flow selected earlier alone; rows count also in a list that does not scroll and are named by their first text; opening something or going home ends the flow; each flow has a serial number, so that a yes for one share never covers another (review 2 C1 and I1, review 4 C2). Test mode checks the recipient of every action that any source rates as sending, whatever its final category (review 2 I2), and a question names a vault's value that the task typed by its kind (`TaskSafety.secrets`; review 2 I3).

## Threads

| Call | Thread | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ScreenTitle`, `ScreenSignature`, `ScreenTree`, `NamePick`, `SafetyCheck`, `LinkCheck`, `TaskAllowance`, `ConfirmationBuilder`, `SendCheck`, `SelfChats`, `AgentFreeApps`, `ToolArguments`, `ActionMapper.proposal`, `screenAction`, `press` and `swipeRefusal`, `Changes`, `StepResult` | any | pure: no I/O, no clock, no shared state |
| `ObservationBuilder`, `ActionMapper.runData` | the task's coroutine | the builder writes to the task's vault through its `Redactor`, and `runData` suspends on `DataPort` (review 3 nit 2) |
| `Redactor`, `Vault` | the task's coroutine | one per task; not thread-safe; the vault is cleared in the task's `finally` |
| the ports (`ScreenPort`, `DataPort`, `OwnerPort`, `ModelPort`, `AppsPort`, `TaskLog`, `EyesPort`) | suspend functions on the agent's coroutine | plans 5B and 5C implement them and choose their own dispatchers |
| the adapters of `:core:providers` | as today (`ProviderHttp` on `Dispatchers.IO`) | the new fields change only the request's body |

**Files:**
- Modify: `settings.gradle.kts`, `core/screen/build.gradle.kts`
- Create: `core/screen-model/build.gradle.kts`, `core/agent/build.gradle.kts`, `core/datatools/build.gradle.kts`, `core/datatools/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `core/perception/build.gradle.kts`, `core/perception/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `core/agent/src/testFixtures/kotlin/dev/kestrel/agent/testing/Fixtures.kt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ScreenSnapshot`, `ScreenElement`, `WindowSummary`, `WindowKind`, `ElementAction`, `IntRect` and `ScreenJson` as they are at `366d867`; `LabelMatcher`, `MatchCandidate`, `MatchDecision`, `Normalizer`, `Strictness` of `:core:commands`.
- Produces (package `dev.kestrel.screen.model`, module `:core:screen-model`): `@Serializable enum class ScrollAxis { VERTICAL, HORIZONTAL }`; `ScreenElement.tooltip: String? = null` and `ScreenElement.scrollAxis: ScrollAxis? = null` (its two last parameters); `@Serializable enum class Region(val label: String)` with `Region.of(bounds: IntRect, area: IntRect): Region`; `object ScreenTree { fun frontWindow(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): WindowSummary?; fun appWindows(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): List<WindowSummary>; fun ancestors(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): List<Int>; fun insideScrollable(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean; fun isVerticalList(element: ScreenElement): Boolean; fun insideVerticalList(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean; fun inToolbar(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean; fun name(element: ScreenElement): String?; fun idName(viewId: String?): String?; fun visibleArea(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, window: WindowSummary): IntRect }`; `object ScreenTitle { const val TOP_BAND = 0.15; fun of(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, window: WindowSummary, appLabel: String?, withRule3: Boolean = true): String? }`; `data class TitleRule(val packageName: String, val titleIds: List<String> = emptyList(), val headerBand: Double? = null)`; `object ScreenTitles { val RULES: List<TitleRule>; fun ruleFor(packageName: String?): TitleRule? }`; `@Serializable data class SignaturePart(val className: String?, val viewId: String?, val region: Region, val count: Int)`; `@Serializable data class Signature(val packageName: String?, val windowId: Int?, val windowKind: WindowKind?, val parts: List<SignaturePart>)` with `similarity(other)` and `sameScreen(other)` (the same package and window kind and parts at least 80 % alike; the window's ID does not count); `object ScreenSignature { const val SAME = 0.8; fun of(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): Signature }`. Package `dev.kestrel.commands.text`: `sealed interface Pick<out T> { One, Several, None }`, `object NamePick { const val MAX_CHOICES = 4; fun <T> pick(spoken: String, items: List<T>, name: (T) -> String, preferred: (T) -> Boolean): Pick<T> }`. Package `dev.kestrel.agent.testing` (test fixtures of `:core:agent`): `object Fixtures { fun screen(name: String): ScreenSnapshot }`. The modules `:core:agent`, `:core:datatools`, `:core:perception`; the anchors of the design's "Shared files and anchors" and `AgentHooks` with its empty command set.

Design D1, D6, D8 and "Shared files and anchors". A plain Kotlin module cannot depend on the Android library `:core:screen`, so the snapshot model moves into the new plain module `:core:screen-model`, in the same package, so that no import changes anywhere; `:core:screen` declares it as `api`. The model gets two fields with defaults, so that `ScreenJson` still reads old files and `FakeNodes` still compiles: `tooltip` (plan 5B fills it from `getTooltipText()`) and `scrollAxis` (plan 5B fills it from `ScrollActions.axis`, mapping its `BOTH` and `UNKNOWN` to null). `ScreenTitle.of` names a screen by D8's four rules; `ScreenSignature.of` describes it without any screen text (D6): the front window's package, ID and kind, and the multiset of (class, view-ID name, 3×3 region, measured above the keyboard) of its elements outside every scrollable container, two of which are the same screen when they have the same package and window kind and their weighted Jaccard similarity is at least 0.8 (the window's ID does not count, because Android gives every window instance a new one), so that a "typing…" line or a Send button in place of the microphone is still the same chat, while apps without view IDs still tell a chat list from a chat. `ScreenTree` holds the questions about the tree that both the safety check and the agent ask. `NamePick` is `AppCommands`' former `pick`, unchanged, so that `open_app` and "open <app>" share one rule. The anchors are comment lines below which plans 5B and 5C insert, so that the two plans never change the same lines.

Create `core/screen-model/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/model/TestScreen.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

/**
 * Builds small snapshots for the tests: one window of 1000 × 2000 pixels and its elements, in the order of [add]. An
 * element is 100 pixels high and as wide as the window unless the test says otherwise; its view ID is written as
 * `<package>:id/<id>` unless it already holds `:id/`. With [keyboardTop], a keyboard window covers the window from there
 * down.
 */
internal class TestScreen(
    private val packageName: String = "dev.example",
    private val windowTitle: String? = null,
    private val windowId: Int = 1,
    private val keyboardTop: Int? = null,
) {
    private val elements = mutableListOf<ScreenElement>()

    fun add(
        top: Int,
        text: String? = null,
        id: String? = null,
        parent: Int? = null,
        className: String = "android.widget.TextView",
        left: Int = 0,
        right: Int = 1000,
        height: Int = 100,
        clickable: Boolean = false,
        editable: Boolean = false,
        scrollable: Boolean = false,
        description: String? = null,
        axis: ScrollAxis? = null,
        actions: Set<ElementAction> = emptySet(),
    ): Int {
        elements += ScreenElement(
            key = "$packageName|${elements.size}",
            windowId = windowId,
            parent = parent,
            packageName = packageName,
            className = className,
            text = text,
            contentDescription = description,
            viewId = id?.let { if (":id/" in it) it else "$packageName:id/$it" },
            label = text ?: description,
            bounds = IntRect(left, top, right, top + height),
            actions = actions,
            clickable = clickable,
            editable = editable,
            scrollable = scrollable,
            scrollAxis = axis,
        )
        return elements.lastIndex
    }

    fun window(): WindowSummary =
        WindowSummary(windowId, WindowKind.APPLICATION, packageName, windowTitle, IntRect(0, 0, 1000, 2000), active = true)

    fun snapshot(): ScreenSnapshot {
        val keyboard = keyboardTop?.let { WindowSummary(99, WindowKind.INPUT_METHOD, "com.example.keyboard", null, IntRect(0, it, 1000, 2000), layer = 2) }
        return ScreenSnapshot(0, listOfNotNull(keyboard, window()), elements.toList())
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class ScreenTreeTest {
    private val area = IntRect(0, 0, 900, 1800)

    @Test
    fun aRegionIsTheCentresCellInAThreeByThreeGrid() {
        assertEquals(Region.TOP_LEFT, Region.of(IntRect(0, 0, 100, 100), area))
        assertEquals(Region.MIDDLE, Region.of(IntRect(400, 850, 500, 950), area))
        assertEquals(Region.BOTTOM_RIGHT, Region.of(IntRect(800, 1700, 900, 1800), area))
        // A centre outside the area takes the nearest cell.
        assertEquals(Region.TOP, Region.of(IntRect(400, -300, 500, -100), area))
        assertEquals("bottom-left", Region.of(IntRect(0, 1700, 100, 1800), area).label)
    }

    @Test
    fun theFrontWindowIsTheActiveAppWindow() {
        val bounds = IntRect(0, 0, 100, 100)
        val keyboard = WindowSummary(3, WindowKind.INPUT_METHOD, "ime", bounds = bounds, active = false)
        val first = WindowSummary(1, WindowKind.APPLICATION, "a", bounds = bounds)
        val active = WindowSummary(2, WindowKind.APPLICATION, "b", bounds = bounds, active = true)

        assertEquals(active, ScreenTree.frontWindow(ScreenSnapshot(0, listOf(keyboard, first, active), emptyList())))
        assertEquals(first, ScreenTree.frontWindow(ScreenSnapshot(0, listOf(keyboard, first), emptyList())))
        assertNull(ScreenTree.frontWindow(ScreenSnapshot(0, listOf(keyboard), emptyList())))
    }

    @Test
    fun aVerticalListIsKnownByItsAxisItsActionsOrItsClass() {
        val screen = TestScreen()
        val vertical = screen.add(0, scrollable = true, axis = ScrollAxis.VERTICAL)
        val row = screen.add(100, text = "Row", parent = vertical)
        val pager = screen.add(200, scrollable = true, axis = ScrollAxis.HORIZONTAL)
        val page = screen.add(300, text = "Page", parent = pager)
        val down = screen.add(400, scrollable = true, actions = setOf(ElementAction.SCROLL_DOWN))
        val recycler = screen.add(500, scrollable = true, className = "androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView")
        val carousel = screen.add(600, scrollable = true, className = "android.widget.HorizontalScrollView")
        val snapshot = screen.snapshot()

        assertTrue(ScreenTree.insideVerticalList(snapshot, row))
        assertFalse(ScreenTree.insideVerticalList(snapshot, page))
        assertTrue(ScreenTree.insideScrollable(snapshot, page))
        assertTrue(ScreenTree.isVerticalList(snapshot.elements[down]))
        assertTrue(ScreenTree.isVerticalList(snapshot.elements[recycler]))
        assertFalse(ScreenTree.isVerticalList(snapshot.elements[carousel]))
        assertEquals(listOf(vertical), ScreenTree.ancestors(snapshot, row))
    }

    @Test
    fun aToolbarIsAViewIdThatHoldsToolbarOrActionBar() {
        val screen = TestScreen()
        val bar = screen.add(0, id = "action_bar_container")
        val title = screen.add(10, text = "Chats", parent = bar)
        val body = screen.add(500, text = "Body", id = "body")
        val snapshot = screen.snapshot()

        assertTrue(ScreenTree.inToolbar(snapshot, title))
        assertFalse(ScreenTree.inToolbar(snapshot, body))
        assertEquals("body", ScreenTree.idName(snapshot.elements[body].viewId))
        assertEquals("search_box", ScreenTree.idName("search_box"))
    }

    @Test
    fun theNewFieldsAreReadFromOldFilesAndKeptWhenSet() {
        val old = """{"takenAtMillis":1,"windows":[],"elements":[{"key":"k","windowId":1,"bounds":{"left":0,"top":0,"right":10,"bottom":10}}]}"""
        val element = ScreenJson.decode(old).elements.single()

        assertNull(element.tooltip)
        assertNull(element.scrollAxis)
        val set = ScreenSnapshot(1, emptyList(), listOf(element.copy(tooltip = "More options", scrollAxis = ScrollAxis.HORIZONTAL)))
        assertEquals(set, ScreenJson.decode(ScreenJson.encode(set)))
        assertFalse("tooltip" in ScreenJson.encode(ScreenSnapshot(1, emptyList(), listOf(element))))
    }

    @Test
    fun theModelPrintsOnlyCountsAndLengthsNeverScreenText() {
        val marker = "Secret483920"
        val element = ScreenElement(
            key = marker, windowId = 1, packageName = marker, className = marker, text = marker, contentDescription = marker, hint = marker,
            supplementalDescription = marker, stateDescription = marker, viewId = marker, label = marker, suggestedName = marker,
            bounds = IntRect(0, 0, 10, 10), tooltip = marker,
        )
        val window = WindowSummary(1, WindowKind.APPLICATION, marker, marker, IntRect(0, 0, 10, 10))
        val printed = listOf(element.toString(), window.toString(), ScreenSnapshot(1, listOf(window), listOf(element)).toString())

        assertTrue(printed.none { marker in it })
        assertEquals("ScreenSnapshot(windows=1, elements=1)", printed[2])
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
import org.junit.Test

class ScreenTitleTest {
    private fun title(screen: TestScreen, appLabel: String?, withRule3: Boolean = true) =
        ScreenTitle.of(screen.snapshot(), screen.window(), appLabel, withRule3)

    @Test
    fun theToolbarNamesTheChatWhenTheWindowTitleIsTheAppsName() {
        val screen = TestScreen(windowTitle = "Kestrel fixtures")
        val bar = screen.add(80, id = "toolbar")
        screen.add(80, description = "Navigate up", parent = bar, right = 100, clickable = true)
        screen.add(90, text = "Ana Petrović", parent = bar, left = 120)
        val list = screen.add(300, scrollable = true, height = 1500)
        screen.add(400, text = "See you tomorrow!", parent = list)

        assertEquals("Ana Petrović", title(screen, "Kestrel fixtures"))
        assertEquals("Ana Petrović", title(screen, "Kestrel fixtures", withRule3 = false))
    }

    @Test
    fun telegramsHeaderIsTheFirstTextInItsBandWithoutViewIds() {
        val screen = TestScreen(packageName = "org.telegram.messenger", windowTitle = "Telegram")
        screen.add(100, description = "Go back", right = 120, clickable = true, className = "android.widget.ImageView")
        screen.add(100, text = "Saved Messages", left = 200, height = 50)
        screen.add(160, text = "forward here to save", left = 200, height = 40)
        val list = screen.add(260, scrollable = true, height = 1500)
        screen.add(300, text = "Shopping list", parent = list)

        assertEquals("Saved Messages", title(screen, "Telegram", withRule3 = false))
    }

    @Test
    fun theMessengerFixtureNamesItsChatByItsViewId() {
        val screen = TestScreen(packageName = "dev.kestrel.testapp", windowTitle = "Kestrel fixtures")
        val bar = screen.add(0, id = "toolbar")
        screen.add(10, text = "Messenger", parent = bar)
        screen.add(500, text = "Ana", id = "chat_title")

        assertEquals("Ana", title(screen, "Kestrel fixtures"))
    }

    @Test
    fun aTitleIdCountsOnlyInTheTopBandOutsideLists() {
        val screen = TestScreen(windowTitle = "Settings")
        val list = screen.add(100, scrollable = true, height = 1800)
        val row = screen.add(150, parent = list, clickable = true)
        screen.add(160, text = "Wi-Fi", id = "android:id/title", parent = row)

        // Rule 3 would take the row's text, so a recipient that leaves rule 3 out has no title here.
        assertEquals("Wi-Fi", title(screen, "Settings"))
        assertNull(title(screen, "Settings", withRule3 = false))

        screen.add(120, text = "Marko", id = "conversation_title", left = 200, height = 50)
        assertEquals("Marko", title(screen, "Settings", withRule3 = false))
    }

    @Test
    fun theWindowTitleCountsOnlyWhenItDiffersFromAKnownAppLabel() {
        val screen = TestScreen(packageName = "com.google.android.gm", windowTitle = "Compose")
        screen.add(1500, text = "Send", clickable = true)

        assertEquals("Compose", title(screen, "Gmail"))
        assertNull(title(screen, "compose"))
        assertNull(title(screen, null))
    }

    @Test
    fun aViberLikeChatIsNamedByItsToolbarOrItsWindowTitle() {
        val toolbar = TestScreen(packageName = "com.viber.voip", windowTitle = "Viber")
        val bar = toolbar.add(80, id = "toolbar")
        toolbar.add(90, text = "My Notes", parent = bar)
        assertEquals("My Notes", title(toolbar, "Viber", withRule3 = false))

        val window = TestScreen(packageName = "com.viber.voip", windowTitle = "Ana")
        window.add(1500, text = "Hello", clickable = true)
        assertEquals("Ana", title(window, "Viber", withRule3 = false))
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class ScreenSignatureTest {
    private val button = "android.widget.ImageButton"
    private val text = "android.widget.TextView"

    /**
     * A chat with view IDs: eleven parts outside the list of messages. With the [keyboard] up, the app's list shrinks and
     * its bottom bar sits just above the keyboard, while its window keeps its full height.
     */
    private fun chat(subtitle: String, sendInsteadOfMic: Boolean, rows: Int = 3, keyboard: Boolean = false): ScreenSnapshot {
        val screen = TestScreen(packageName = "com.example.chat", keyboardTop = if (keyboard) 1200 else null)
        val bar = if (keyboard) 1100 else 1800
        screen.add(80, id = "back", className = button, right = 100, clickable = true)
        screen.add(80, id = "avatar", className = "android.widget.ImageView", left = 100, right = 200)
        screen.add(80, text = "Ana", id = "title", left = 220, right = 600, height = 50)
        screen.add(130, text = subtitle, id = "subtitle", left = 220, right = 600, height = 40)
        screen.add(80, id = "call", className = button, left = 700, right = 800, clickable = true)
        screen.add(80, id = "menu", className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)
        val list = screen.add(250, id = "messages", className = "androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView", height = bar - 350, scrollable = true)
        repeat(rows) { screen.add(300 + it * 100, text = "Message $it", id = "bubble", parent = list) }
        screen.add(bar, id = "emoji", className = button, right = 100, clickable = true)
        screen.add(bar, id = "compose", className = "android.widget.EditText", left = 100, right = 700, editable = true)
        screen.add(bar, id = "attach", className = button, left = 700, right = 800, clickable = true)
        screen.add(bar, id = if (sendInsteadOfMic) "send" else "mic", className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)
        return screen.snapshot()
    }

    @Test
    fun aTypingLineOrASendButtonInPlaceOfTheMicrophoneIsTheSameScreen() {
        val before = ScreenSignature.of(chat("online", sendInsteadOfMic = false))
        val after = ScreenSignature.of(chat("typing…", sendInsteadOfMic = true))

        assertTrue(before.sameScreen(after))
        assertEquals("com.example.chat", before.packageName)
    }

    @Test
    fun theKeyboardNeverMovesTheBarAboveItToAnotherRegion() {
        val before = ScreenSignature.of(chat("online", sendInsteadOfMic = false))
        val after = ScreenSignature.of(chat("online", sendInsteadOfMic = false, keyboard = true))

        assertEquals(before.parts, after.parts)
        assertTrue(before.sameScreen(after))
    }

    @Test
    fun rowsOfAListDoNotCount() {
        assertEquals(ScreenSignature.of(chat("online", false, rows = 3)), ScreenSignature.of(chat("online", false, rows = 9)))
    }

    @Test
    fun anAppWithoutViewIdsStillTellsItsChatListFromAChat() {
        val list = TestScreen(packageName = "org.telegram.messenger")
        list.add(80, className = button, right = 100, clickable = true)
        list.add(80, text = "Telegram", left = 200, right = 600)
        list.add(80, className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)
        list.add(250, className = "androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView", height = 1450, scrollable = true)
        list.add(1800, className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)
        val chat = TestScreen(packageName = "org.telegram.messenger")
        chat.add(80, className = button, right = 100, clickable = true)
        chat.add(80, className = "android.widget.ImageView", left = 100, right = 200)
        chat.add(80, text = "Ana", left = 220, right = 600, height = 50)
        chat.add(130, text = "online", left = 220, right = 600, height = 40)
        chat.add(80, className = button, left = 700, right = 800, clickable = true)
        chat.add(80, className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)
        chat.add(250, className = "androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView", height = 1450, scrollable = true)
        chat.add(1800, className = button, right = 100, clickable = true)
        chat.add(1800, className = "android.widget.EditText", left = 100, right = 700, editable = true)
        chat.add(1800, className = button, left = 700, right = 800, clickable = true)
        chat.add(1800, className = button, left = 900, clickable = true)

        assertFalse(ScreenSignature.of(list.snapshot()).sameScreen(ScreenSignature.of(chat.snapshot())))
    }

    @Test
    fun anotherPackageIsAnotherScreenButAnotherWindowOfTheSameShapeIsNot() {
        val first = TestScreen(packageName = "com.example.a")
        first.add(100, text = "Hello", className = text)
        val second = TestScreen(packageName = "com.example.b")
        second.add(100, text = "Hello", className = text)
        val window = TestScreen(packageName = "com.example.a", windowId = 2)
        window.add(100, text = "Hello", className = text)
        val signature = ScreenSignature.of(first.snapshot())

        assertTrue(signature.sameScreen(ScreenSignature.of(first.snapshot())))
        assertFalse(signature.sameScreen(ScreenSignature.of(second.snapshot())))
        // Android gives every window instance a new ID, also the same screen after its app restarted (design D23).
        assertTrue(signature.sameScreen(ScreenSignature.of(window.snapshot())))
    }

    @Test
    fun theSimilarityCountsEachPartAsOftenAsItOccurs() {
        val one = TestScreen()
        one.add(100, className = button, clickable = true)
        val two = TestScreen()
        two.add(100, className = button, clickable = true)
        two.add(100, className = button, clickable = true)

        assertEquals(0.5, ScreenSignature.of(one.snapshot()).similarity(ScreenSignature.of(two.snapshot())), 1e-9)
        assertEquals(1.0, Signature(null, null, null, emptyList()).similarity(Signature(null, null, null, emptyList())), 1e-9)
    }
}
```

Create `core/commands/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/commands/text/NamePickTest.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.commands.text

import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Test

class NamePickTest {
    private class App(val label: String, val work: Boolean)

    private val chrome = App("Chrome", work = false)
    private val workChrome = App("Chrome", work = true)
    private val gmail = App("Gmail", work = false)
    private val clock = App("Clock", work = false)
    private val photos = App("Photos", work = false)
    private val editor = App("Photo Editor", work = false)
    private val apps = listOf(workChrome, chrome, gmail, clock, photos, editor, App("Phone", work = false))

    private fun pick(spoken: String, items: List<App> = apps) = NamePick.pick(spoken, items, { it.label }, { !it.work })

    @Test
    fun theOwnersAppStandsForTheSameAppInTheWorkProfile() {
        assertEquals(Pick.One(gmail), pick("Gmail"))
        assertEquals(Pick.One(chrome), pick("chrome"))
        assertEquals(Pick.One(workChrome), pick("Chrome", listOf(workChrome, gmail)))
        assertEquals(Pick.None, pick("Quorbex Zyntal"))
    }

    @Test
    fun twoAppsOfTheOwnerWithTheSameNameAreBothOffered() {
        val otherPhone = App("Phone", work = false)
        val phone = App("Phone", work = false)

        assertEquals(Pick.Several(listOf(phone, otherPhone)), pick("Phone", listOf(phone, otherPhone, gmail)))
    }

    @Test
    fun closeNamesAreOfferedAndAtMostFourOfThem() {
        assertEquals(Pick.Several(listOf(photos, editor)), pick("Photo"))
        val many = (1..6).map { App("Notes $it", work = false) }
        assertEquals(NamePick.MAX_CHOICES, (pick("Notes", many) as Pick.Several).items.size)
    }
}
```

```kotlin
// The agent's loop, observation, tools, memory and routines (design D1 of sub-project 5). Its test fixtures hold the
// scripted model and the fakes, which :app's debug build uses too, so they use only Kotlin, coroutines and
// kotlinx.serialization: the audit checks the debug runtime classpath.
dependencies {
    api(project(":core:screen-model"))
    api(project(":core:safety"))
    api(project(":core:providers"))
    implementation(project(":core:commands"))
    api(libs.kotlinx.coroutines.core)
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/**
 * Where an element lies in a window, in a 3×3 grid (design D6 and D8 of sub-project 5): the observation's `@top-left`
 * to `@bottom-right` and a part of the screen signature. Never coordinates.
 */
@Serializable
enum class Region(val label: String) {
    TOP_LEFT("top-left"),
    TOP("top"),
    TOP_RIGHT("top-right"),
    LEFT("left"),
    MIDDLE("middle"),
    RIGHT("right"),
    BOTTOM_LEFT("bottom-left"),
    BOTTOM("bottom"),
    BOTTOM_RIGHT("bottom-right"),
    ;

    companion object {
        /** The cell of [area] that holds the centre of [bounds]; a centre outside [area] takes the nearest cell. */
        fun of(bounds: IntRect, area: IntRect): Region {
            if (area.isEmpty) return MIDDLE
            val column = ((bounds.centerX - area.left).toLong() * 3 / area.width).toInt().coerceIn(0, 2)
            val row = ((bounds.centerY - area.top).toLong() * 3 / area.height).toInt().coerceIn(0, 2)
            return entries[row * 3 + column]
        }
    }
}

/** Plain questions about a snapshot's tree that the agent and the safety check both ask (design D1 of sub-project 5). */
object ScreenTree {
    private val VERTICAL_CLASSES = listOf("RecyclerView", "ListView", "ScrollView", "GridView")

    /** The active app window, else the first app window, else null. */
    fun frontWindow(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): WindowSummary? {
        val apps = appWindows(snapshot)
        return apps.firstOrNull { it.active } ?: apps.firstOrNull()
    }

    /** Every app window, both apps of a split screen included. */
    fun appWindows(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): List<WindowSummary> = snapshot.windows.filter { it.kind == WindowKind.APPLICATION }

    /**
     * The part of [window] that the app can use: its bounds with the bottom raised to the top of a keyboard that covers its
     * lower half. The window keeps its full height while the keyboard shows, but the app moves its bottom bar above the
     * keyboard, so regions measured in this area do not change when the keyboard opens or closes (design D6).
     */
    fun visibleArea(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, window: WindowSummary): IntRect {
        val bounds = window.bounds
        val top = snapshot.windows.filter { it.kind == WindowKind.INPUT_METHOD }
            .mapNotNull { it.bounds.intersect(bounds) }
            .filter { it.centerY > bounds.centerY }
            .minOfOrNull { it.top } ?: return bounds
        return if (top > bounds.top) bounds.copy(bottom = top) else bounds
    }

    /** The indices of the ancestors of element [index], nearest first. */
    fun ancestors(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): List<Int> = buildList {
        val seen = HashSet<Int>()
        var parent = snapshot.elements.getOrNull(index)?.parent
        while (parent != null && seen.add(parent)) {
            add(parent)
            parent = snapshot.elements.getOrNull(parent)?.parent
        }
    }

    fun insideScrollable(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean =
        ancestors(snapshot, index).any { snapshot.elements[it].scrollable }

    /**
     * Whether [element] is a list that scrolls up and down: by its axis, else by its up or down action, else by a class
     * of a vertical list. A horizontal scroll view, a pager or a carousel is none.
     */
    fun isVerticalList(element: ScreenElement): Boolean {
        if (!element.scrollable) return false
        element.scrollAxis?.let { return it == ScrollAxis.VERTICAL }
        val actions = element.actions
        if (ElementAction.SCROLL_UP in actions || ElementAction.SCROLL_DOWN in actions) return true
        if (ElementAction.SCROLL_LEFT in actions || ElementAction.SCROLL_RIGHT in actions) return false
        val name = element.className.orEmpty()
        return !name.endsWith("HorizontalScrollView") && VERTICAL_CLASSES.any { name.endsWith(it) }
    }

    fun insideVerticalList(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean =
        ancestors(snapshot, index).any { isVerticalList(snapshot.elements[it]) }

    /** Whether element [index] or an ancestor has a view ID that holds `toolbar` or `action_bar`. */
    fun inToolbar(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, index: Int): Boolean =
        (listOf(index) + ancestors(snapshot, index)).any { position ->
            val id = idName(snapshot.elements[position].viewId)?.lowercase() ?: return@any false
            "toolbar" in id || "action_bar" in id
        }

    /** The element's label, else the name that Kestrel derived from its view ID. */
    fun name(element: ScreenElement): String? = element.label ?: element.suggestedName

    /** The part of a view ID after `:id/`; a Firefox page's HTML `id` has none and stays whole. */
    fun idName(viewId: String?): String? = viewId?.substringAfter(":id/")?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

/**
 * An app's own rule for the title of its screens (design D8 of sub-project 5): the view-ID names of the header's title
 * ([titleIds], the part after `:id/`, in order of preference), or for an app without view IDs the top fraction of the
 * window ([headerBand]) in which the first text outside every scrollable container is the header.
 */
data class TitleRule(val packageName: String, val titleIds: List<String> = emptyList(), val headerBand: Double? = null)

/**
 * The apps' title rules, rule 1 of [ScreenTitle]. Plan 5B adds the emulator's entries from the trees that its device
 * tests record, and the controller the A71's after the owner's first sitting (design D8 and D30). Viber gets none until
 * a tree of the real Viber app is recorded (the owner's answer to Q1).
 */
object ScreenTitles {
    val RULES: List<TitleRule> = listOf(
        // Telegram draws its chat header without view IDs (research r63): the title is the first text of the header.
        TitleRule("org.telegram.messenger", headerBand = 0.12),
        TitleRule("org.telegram.messenger.web", headerBand = 0.12),
        // :testapp's messenger (plan 5B) names its chat header `chat_title`.
        TitleRule("dev.kestrel.testapp", titleIds = listOf("chat_title")),
        // sub-project 5B: entries
    )

    fun ruleFor(packageName: String?): TitleRule? = RULES.firstOrNull { it.packageName == packageName }
}
```

Create `core/screen-model/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/model/ScreenTitle.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

/**
 * The title of a screen (design D8 of sub-project 5). Android's window title is usually the activity's or the app's
 * label ("Telegram" on every chat), so it comes last. The rules, in order:
 * 1. the app's rule in [ScreenTitles];
 * 2. a text in the window's toolbar or action bar, or an element whose view ID holds "title" in the top band of the
 *    window outside every scrollable container (a chat header, never a list row such as `android:id/title`);
 * 3. with `withRule3`, the first text without an action in the top band, which can be a list's first row or a clock, so
 *    a recipient (design D14) and "another screen" (design D6) leave it out;
 * 4. the window's title, only when it differs from the app's launcher label, and only when the caller knows that label.
 * No title is a valid answer.
 */
object ScreenTitle {
    /** The top part of the window in which rules 2 and 3 look: 15 % of its height. */
    const val TOP_BAND = 0.15

    fun of(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, window: WindowSummary, appLabel: String?, withRule3: Boolean = true): String? {
        val elements = snapshot.elements
        val inWindow = elements.indices.filter { elements[it].windowId == window.id }
            .sortedWith(compareBy({ elements[it].bounds.top }, { elements[it].bounds.left }))
        ScreenTitles.ruleFor(window.packageName)?.let { rule -> byRule(snapshot, window, rule, inWindow)?.let { return it } }
        val band = window.bounds.top + window.bounds.height * TOP_BAND
        fun inBand(element: ScreenElement) = element.bounds.centerY < band
        inWindow.firstOrNull { index ->
            val element = elements[index]
            val titleId = ScreenTree.idName(element.viewId)?.contains("title", ignoreCase = true) == true
            text(element) != null && !element.editable &&
                (ScreenTree.inToolbar(snapshot, index) || (titleId && inBand(element) && !ScreenTree.insideScrollable(snapshot, index)))
        }?.let { return text(elements[it]) }
        if (withRule3) {
            inWindow.firstOrNull { index ->
                val element = elements[index]
                text(element) != null && !element.isActionable && !element.editable && inBand(element)
            }?.let { return text(elements[it]) }
        }
        val title = window.title?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() } ?: return null
        if (appLabel == null || title.equals(appLabel.trim(), ignoreCase = true)) return null
        return title
    }

    private fun byRule(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot, window: WindowSummary, rule: TitleRule, inWindow: List<Int>): String? {
        val elements = snapshot.elements
        for (id in rule.titleIds) {
            inWindow.firstOrNull { ScreenTree.idName(elements[it].viewId) == id }?.let { index -> named(elements[index])?.let { return it } }
        }
        val fraction = rule.headerBand ?: return null
        val bottom = window.bounds.top + window.bounds.height * fraction
        return inWindow.firstOrNull { index ->
            val element = elements[index]
            text(element) != null && !element.editable && element.bounds.centerY < bottom && !ScreenTree.insideScrollable(snapshot, index)
        }?.let { text(elements[it]) }
    }

    private fun text(element: ScreenElement): String? = element.text?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }

    private fun named(element: ScreenElement): String? =
        listOf(element.text, element.contentDescription, element.label).firstNotNullOfOrNull { it?.trim()?.takeIf(String::isNotEmpty) }
}
```

Create `core/screen-model/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/screen/model/ScreenSignature.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.screen.model

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

/** One kind of element of a screen signature and how often it occurs: no screen text. */
@Serializable
data class SignaturePart(val className: String?, val viewId: String?, val region: Region, val count: Int)

/**
 * A screen's shape without its text (design D6 of sub-project 5): the front app's package, its active window's ID and
 * kind, and the multiset of (class, view-ID name, region) of the elements outside every scrollable container, with the
 * regions measured above the keyboard ([ScreenTree.visibleArea]). Routines store it, so it holds no label.
 */
@Serializable
data class Signature(val packageName: String?, val windowId: Int?, val windowKind: WindowKind?, val parts: List<SignaturePart>) {
    /** The weighted Jaccard similarity of the two multisets: the counts matter, not only which parts occur. */
    fun similarity(other: Signature): Double {
        val mine = parts.associate { Triple(it.className, it.viewId, it.region) to it.count }
        val theirs = other.parts.associate { Triple(it.className, it.viewId, it.region) to it.count }
        val keys = mine.keys + theirs.keys
        if (keys.isEmpty()) return 1.0
        val shared = keys.sumOf { minOf(mine[it] ?: 0, theirs[it] ?: 0) }
        val all = keys.sumOf { maxOf(mine[it] ?: 0, theirs[it] ?: 0) }
        return shared.toDouble() / all
    }

    /**
     * The same app and window kind, and parts at least [ScreenSignature.SAME] alike. The window's ID does not count:
     * Android gives every window instance a new one, also the same screen after its app's process restarted, so a routine
     * recorded in an earlier session could never match (design D23). Within one step a new window is another screen
     * (design D6), so the step's own comparisons (`Changes`, the observation's stars) compare [windowId] as well.
     */
    fun sameScreen(other: Signature): Boolean =
        packageName == other.packageName && windowKind == other.windowKind && similarity(other) + 1e-9 >= ScreenSignature.SAME

    override fun toString(): String = "Signature(packageLength=${packageName?.length ?: 0}, kind=$windowKind, parts=${parts.size})"
}

object ScreenSignature {
    /** Two signatures at least this alike are the same screen (design D6 of sub-project 5). */
    const val SAME = 0.8

    fun of(snapshot: ScreenSnapshot): Signature {
        val window = ScreenTree.frontWindow(snapshot) ?: return Signature(null, null, null, emptyList())
        val area = ScreenTree.visibleArea(snapshot, window)
        val counts = snapshot.elements.indices
            .filter { snapshot.elements[it].windowId == window.id && !ScreenTree.insideScrollable(snapshot, it) }
            .map { snapshot.elements[it] }
            .groupingBy { Triple(it.className, ScreenTree.idName(it.viewId), Region.of(it.bounds, area)) }
            .eachCount()
        val parts = counts.map { (key, count) -> SignaturePart(key.first, key.second, key.third, count) }
            .sortedWith(compareBy({ it.region.ordinal }, { it.className.orEmpty() }, { it.viewId.orEmpty() }))
        return Signature(window.packageName, window.id, window.kind, parts)
    }
}
```

Create `core/commands/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/commands/text/NamePick.kt`:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.commands.text

/** What the owner named: one item, several close ones for "Which one?", or none. */
sealed interface Pick<out T> {
    data class One<T>(val item: T) : Pick<T>

    data class Several<T>(val items: List<T>) : Pick<T>

    data object None : Pick<Nothing>
}

/**
 * The matcher of "open <app>" and of the agent's `open_app` (design D1 and D11 of sub-project 5), moved unchanged from
 * `:app`'s `AppCommands.kt` so that both share one rule (design spec, section 9.6).
 */
object NamePick {
    /** How many names "Which one?" offers at most. */
    const val MAX_CHOICES = 4

    /**
     * The item whose [name] the owner said in [spoken], with the matcher's normal limits. Among items with the same name,
     * the [preferred] ones stand for the others, as an app of the owner's profile does for the same app in the work
     * profile; two preferred items with the same name both stay, for "Which one?". A single near miss gets "Which one?"
     * too, with its one name.
     */
    fun <T> pick(spoken: String, items: List<T>, name: (T) -> String, preferred: (T) -> Boolean): Pick<T> {
        val distinct = items.filter { Normalizer.normalize(name(it)).isNotEmpty() }
            .groupBy { Normalizer.normalize(name(it)) }
            .values.flatMap { same -> same.filter(preferred).ifEmpty { same } }
        val candidates = distinct.mapIndexed { index, item -> MatchCandidate(index.toString(), listOf(name(item))) }
        return when (val decision = LabelMatcher.decide(spoken, candidates, Strictness.NORMAL)) {
            is MatchDecision.Found -> Pick.One(distinct[decision.id.toInt()])
            is MatchDecision.Ambiguous -> Pick.Several(decision.ids.take(MAX_CHOICES).map { distinct[it.toInt()] })
            MatchDecision.NotFound -> Pick.None
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
/** What the owner named: one item, several close ones for "Which one?", or none. */
internal sealed interface Pick<out T> {
    data class One<T>(val item: T) : Pick<T>

    data class Several<T>(val items: List<T>) : Pick<T>

    data object None : Pick<Nothing>
}

/** How many names "Which one?" says aloud at most. */
internal const val MAX_SPOKEN_CHOICES = 4

/**
 * The item whose [name] the owner said in [spoken], with the matcher's normal limits (design spec, section 9.6). Among
 * items with the same name, the [preferred] ones stand for the others, as an app of the owner's profile does for the same
 * app in the work profile; two preferred items with the same name both stay, for "Which one?". A single near miss gets
 * "Which one?" too, with its one name, and only its number or its name chooses it; any other answer, "yes" among them,
 * ends the command and is passed on as a new utterance.
 */
internal fun <T> pick(spoken: String, items: List<T>, name: (T) -> String, preferred: (T) -> Boolean): Pick<T> {
    val distinct = items.filter { Normalizer.normalize(name(it)).isNotEmpty() }
        .groupBy { Normalizer.normalize(name(it)) }
        .values.flatMap { same -> same.filter(preferred).ifEmpty { same } }
    val candidates = distinct.mapIndexed { index, item -> MatchCandidate(index.toString(), listOf(name(item))) }
    return when (val decision = LabelMatcher.decide(spoken, candidates, Strictness.NORMAL)) {
        is MatchDecision.Found -> Pick.One(distinct[decision.id.toInt()])
        is MatchDecision.Ambiguous -> Pick.Several(decision.ids.take(MAX_SPOKEN_CHOICES).map { distinct[it.toInt()] })
        MatchDecision.NotFound -> Pick.None
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.app.commands

import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

/** "Which one?" after "open <app>"; the matcher itself is `NamePick` of `:core:commands`, tested in `NamePickTest`. */
class PhoneAppsTest {
    @Test
    fun anAnswerIsANumberOrOneOfTheNames() = runTest {
        val names = listOf("Photos", "Photo Editor")

        assertEquals(Answer.Chosen(1), askAmong(Answers("2"), PhoneCommandTexts.whichOne(names), names))
        assertEquals(Answer.Chosen(1), askAmong(Answers("photo editor"), "Which one?", names))
        assertEquals(Answer.Chosen(1), askAmong(Answers("to"), "Which one?", names))
    }

    @Test
    fun anAnswerThatIsNoChoiceEndsTheCommand() = runTest {
        val names = listOf("Photos", "Photo Editor")

        assertEquals(Answer.Ends(CommandResult(Outcome.CANCELLED, passOn = "scroll down")), askAmong(Answers("scroll down"), "Which one?", names))
        assertEquals(Answer.Ends(CommandResult(Outcome.FAILED, show = PhoneCommandTexts.noChoice(3))), askAmong(Answers("3"), "Which one?", names))
        assertEquals(Answer.Ends(CommandResult(Outcome.CANCELLED)), askAmong(Answers(null), "Which one?", names))
        assertEquals("Which one? 1, Photos. 2, Photo Editor.", PhoneCommandTexts.whichOne(names))
        // Two offered items with the same name: the name chooses neither, and it is no new utterance.
        assertEquals(

            askAmong(Answers("phone"), "Which one?", listOf("Phone", "Phone")),
        )
    }

    /** Answers each question with the next of [answers]; null is a question that nobody answered. */
    private class Answers(private vararg val answers: String?) : CommandConversation {
        private var next = 0

        override suspend fun say(text: String) = Unit

        override suspend fun ask(question: String): String? = answers[next++]

        override fun keep(text: String) = Unit

        override suspend fun countdown(millis: Long, text: (secondsLeft: Int) -> String): Boolean = true
    }
}
```

### Task 2: The provider changes for the agent's requests

**Files:**
- Modify: `core/providers/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/providers/chat/ChatRequest.kt`, `chat/ChatRequests.kt`, `http/ProviderError.kt`, `http/ErrorCodes.kt`, `http/ProviderHttp.kt`, `styles/Adapters.kt`, `styles/AnthropicAdapter.kt`, `styles/ResponsesAdapter.kt`, `styles/ChatCompletionsAdapter.kt`, `styles/GeminiAdapter.kt`, `styles/OllamaAdapter.kt`, `styles/BedrockAdapter.kt`
- Modify: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-kestrel-design.md` (10.3)
- Test: `core/providers/src/test/kotlin/dev/kestrel/providers/chat/ChatRequestsTest.kt`, `http/ErrorCodesTest.kt`, `styles/AgentRequestsTest.kt` (new), fixtures `core/providers/src/test/resources/fixtures/anthropic/agent.request.json`, `responses/agent-copilot.request.json`, `chat-completions/agent-copilot.request.json`, `gemini/agent.request.json` (new)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ChatRequest`, `ChatMessage`, `Part`, `AssistantPart`, `ModelTarget`, `StyleOptions`, `ProviderError`, `ErrorCodes`, `HttpReply`, `ProviderHttp`, `Wire`, `CatalogLoader.COPILOT`, `CompatDefaults.endpointClass`, the adapters and `AdapterHarness` as they are at `366d867`.
- Produces (package `dev.kestrel.providers.chat`): `ChatRequest.context: String? = null`, `ChatRequest.cacheAfter: Int? = null`, `ChatRequest.cacheFields: CacheFields = CacheFields.ALL` (its three last parameters); `@Serializable data class CacheFields(val anthropicMarks: Boolean = true, val responsesExplicit: Boolean = true, val chatCopilotMarks: Boolean = true)` with `CacheFields.ALL` and `CacheFields.NONE`; `ChatRequests.check` refuses a `ToolResult` without an earlier call and a `cacheAfter` outside `messages`. Package `dev.kestrel.providers.http`: `ProviderError.BadRequest(val status: Int, val code: String?, val toolChoice: Boolean = false)`; `ErrorCodes.namesToolChoice(reply: HttpReply): Boolean`. Internal: `Wire.CONTEXT_SEPARATOR`, `Wire.systemAndContext(request)`, `Wire.mergeUsers(messages)`, `Wire.toolUseId(id, chars, max = 64)`.

Design D4, D5 and D32 items 8 and 38. The agent's conversation keeps one fixed prefix for the providers' prompt caches (r51; decision 2): the tools and the system prompt never change, and the per-task text (memory, the test-mode note) follows in the new field `context`, which each style puts right after the system prompt: Anthropic's second system block (also on Vertex and Foundry, whose Claude goes through the same adapter), Bedrock's second system block, Gemini's second part of `systemInstruction`, one system message with the separator line `----` on Chat Completions and Ollama (some servers and Copilot's route to Gemini keep only one system message), and on Responses a `developer` item for the ChatGPT plan and OpenAI's own models (OpenAI's API, Azure OpenAI and Copilot's `/responses`), whose system prompt also goes as a `developer` item for GPT-5.6 and later (r51: on newer models the top-level `instructions` are billed uncached), while the plan keeps `instructions` and every other Responses target (xAI, Foundry's other models, Mantle) gets a second `system` item (review A2-M7). `cacheAfter` names the last message of the part of the conversation that never changes again (D3's stable region): Anthropic marks it as its fourth breakpoint after the last tool, the system prompt and the context; Claude on Bedrock gets cache points in the same places; Copilot's `/responses` for GPT-5.6 and the GPT-6 family (the models that VS Code's client gates, `modelSupportCacheBreakPoints` in r51's source R11) gets `prompt_cache_options: {"mode": "explicit"}` with `prompt_cache_breakpoint: {"mode": "explicit"}` on the system prompt's and the context's content blocks and on the item of that message, in VS Code's shape (r51's source R9), because in explicit mode OpenAI writes cache entries only at breakpoints, and the one on the system prompt lets a new task, whose context differs, read the tools and the system prompt from the cache (the controller's decision on review M3); Copilot's `/chat/completions` gets `copilot_cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` on the system message and on the wire message that holds message `cacheAfter` after adjacent user messages were merged (review A3-N3). A Chat Completions route that takes Anthropic's `cache_control` (`cacheControlFormat == "anthropic"`: OpenRouter's Claude and Gemini, Model Studio, DeepInfra's Claude) gets its one system message as two text blocks, the system prompt and the context, each with `cache_control`, so that the system prompt's cache entry does not change with the task's context. Each of the three Copilot fields can be switched off on its own through `cacheFields`, which travels with the request because `StyleOptions` is built inside `:core:providers` (review A M2). The Chat Completions and Gemini adapters merge adjacent user messages, because some local servers refuse two user turns in a row (review A2-M6). A 400 whose error names the tool choice sets `BadRequest.toolChoice`, computed from the body without keeping any of it (review note R2), so that the agent can send the request once more with `auto` (D4). `ChatRequests.check` refuses a tool result whose ID no earlier call has (D32 item 8), and Chat Completions to OpenAI's and Azure's own hosts rewrites an ID of more than 40 characters as Responses rewrites one of more than 64, so that a history from Responses survives an escalation to an Azure Chat Completions deployment (D32 item 38). Gemini and Ollama get no cache fields (implicit caching), and `prompt_cache_key` stays as it is.

```kotlin
/**
 * The agent's requests in every style (design D4, D5 and D32 items 8 and 38 of sub-project 5): the per-task context
 * after the system prompt, the cache marks at the end of the part that never changes (`cacheAfter`), Copilot's three
 * cache fields and their switches, the merge of adjacent user messages, the tool-choice flag and the 40-character IDs.
 */
class AgentRequestsTest {
    private val bench = AdapterHarness()

    private val context = "Facts the owner saved: home is Main Street 1."

    // The task, the first screen, one shrunk step (its call and result) and the newest observation; message 3 is the
    // last one that never changes again.
    private val history = arrayOf(
        user("Task: open the camera."),
        user("First screen: Launcher."),
        ChatMessage.Assistant(listOf(AssistantPart.ToolCall("call_1", "open_app", obj("""{"name":"Camera"}""")))),
        ChatMessage.ToolResult("call_1", "open_app", "Step 1: opened Camera."),
        user("Observation 2: Camera"),
    )

    private fun agent(fields: CacheFields = CacheFields.ALL): ChatRequest.() -> ChatRequest =
        { copy(context = this@AgentRequestsTest.context, cacheAfter = 3, cacheFields = fields) }

    private fun body(): JsonObject = bench.body(bench.take())

    /** Every object with the key [key] anywhere in [element], so that a test can count the marks. */
    private fun count(element: kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonElement, key: String): Int = when (element) {
        is JsonObject -> (if (key in element) 1 else 0) + element.values.sumOf { count(it, key) }
        is kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonArray -> element.sumOf { count(it, key) }
        else -> 0
    }

    fun close() = bench.close()

        AnthropicAdapter(bench.http).complete(request(*history, block = agent()), anthropic)

        val recorded = bench.take()
        bench.assertBody("anthropic/agent.request.json", recorded)
        // The last tool, the system prompt, the context and message 3: Anthropic's four breakpoints.
        assertEquals(4, count(bench.body(recorded), "cache_control"))
    }

    @Test
    fun azuresChatCompletionsCutTheLongIdsOfAHistoryFromResponses() = runBlocking {
        bench.reply("chat-completions/text.sse")
        bench.reply("chat-completions/text.sse")
        val adapter = ChatCompletionsAdapter(bench.http)
        val long = "fc_" + "a1b2c3d4".repeat(7) + "e5f6g"
        val escalated = arrayOf(
            user("Task: open the camera."),
            ChatMessage.Assistant(listOf(AssistantPart.ToolCall(long, "open_app", obj("""{"name":"Camera"}""")))),
            ChatMessage.ToolResult(long, "open_app", "Opened."),
        )
        val azure = target("azure-openai", RequestStyle.CHAT_COMPLETIONS, "https://kestrel.openai.azure.com/openai/v1", ModelEntry("gpt-6-luna", "GPT-6 Luna"))
        val deepSeek = target("deepseek", RequestStyle.CHAT_COMPLETIONS, "https://api.deepseek.com", ModelEntry("deepseek-v4-flash", "DeepSeek V4 Flash"))

        adapter.complete(request(*escalated), azure)
        adapter.complete(request(*escalated), deepSeek)

        assertEquals(64, long.length)
        val cut = body()["messages"]!!.jsonArray
        val callId = cut[2].jsonObject["tool_calls"]!!.jsonArray[0].jsonObject["id"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content
        assertEquals(40, callId.length)
        assertTrue(callId.startsWith("fc_a1b2c3d4"))
        assertEquals(callId, cut[3].jsonObject["tool_call_id"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content)
        val kept = body()["messages"]!!.jsonArray
        assertEquals(long, kept[3].jsonObject["tool_call_id"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content)
    }

    @Test
    fun claudeOnBedrockGetsCachePointsAndOllamaOneSystemMessage() = runBlocking {
        bench.reply("bedrock/text.json")
        bench.reply("bedrock/text.json")
        bench.reply("ollama/text.json")
        val bedrock = BedrockAdapter(bench.http)
        val claude = target("amazon-bedrock", RequestStyle.BEDROCK, "https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com", ModelEntry("anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-v1:0", "Claude Sonnet 5"))
        val ollama = target("ollama", RequestStyle.OLLAMA, "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1", ModelEntry("qwen3.6", "Qwen3.6"))

        bedrock.complete(request(*history, block = agent()), claude)
        bedrock.complete(request(*history, block = agent(CacheFields.NONE)), claude)
        OllamaAdapter(bench.http).complete(request(*history, block = agent()), ollama)

        val point = json("""{"cachePoint":{"type":"default"}}""")
        val marked = body()
        assertEquals(json("""[{"text":"You are Kestrel."},$point,{"text":"$context"},$point]"""), marked["system"])
        val turns = marked["messages"]!!.jsonArray
        assertEquals(listOf("user", "assistant", "user"), turns.map { it.jsonObject["role"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content })
        assertEquals(point, turns[2].jsonObject["content"]!!.jsonArray[1])
        val unmarked = body()
        assertEquals(json("""[{"text":"You are Kestrel."},$point,{"text":"$context"}]"""), unmarked["system"])
        assertFalse(unmarked["messages"].toString().contains("cachePoint"))
        val local = bench.body(bench.take())["messages"]!!.jsonArray
        assertEquals(json("""{"role":"system","content":"You are Kestrel.\n\n----\n\n$context"}"""), local[0])
    }

    @Test
    fun aBadRequestThatNamesTheToolChoiceIsFlagged() {
        bench.status(400, """{"error": {"message": "Tool choice 'required' is not supported.", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "tool_choice"}}""")
        bench.status(400, """{"error": {"message": "Bad.", "type": "invalid_request_error"}}""")
        val openAi = target("openai", RequestStyle.RESPONSES, "https://api.openai.com/v1", ModelEntry("gpt-5.5", "GPT-5.5"))
        val adapter = ResponsesAdapter(bench.http)

        assertEquals(ProviderError.BadRequest(400, "invalid_request_error", toolChoice = true), errorOf(adapter, request(user("Hi")), openAi))
        assertEquals(ProviderError.BadRequest(400, "invalid_request_error", toolChoice = false), errorOf(adapter, request(user("Hi")), openAi))
        assertEquals("BadRequest(status=400, code=null, toolChoice=true)", ProviderError.BadRequest(400, null, toolChoice = true).toString())
    }
}
```

```kotlin
    val meta: RequestMeta = RequestMeta(),
    /**
     * The per-task text that follows the system prompt (design D5 of sub-project 5): the memory that the task needs and
     * the test-mode note. Each style puts it right after the system prompt, so that the tools and the system prompt stay
     * one cached prefix for every task.
     */
    val context: String? = null,
    /**
     * The index in [messages] of the last message that never changes again (design D3 and D5 of sub-project 5), where the
     * styles that take explicit cache marks put their last one; null for none.
     */
    val cacheAfter: Int? = null,
    /** Which of Copilot's cache fields the request may send (design D5 of sub-project 5). */
    val cacheFields: CacheFields = CacheFields.ALL,
) {
    override fun toString(): String =
        "ChatRequest(systemLength=${system.length}, messages=${messages.size}, tools=${tools.size}, " +
            "toolChoice=$toolChoice, reasoning=$reasoning, maxOutputTokens=$maxOutputTokens, " +
            "temperature=${if (temperature == null) "default" else "set"}, cacheKey=${if (cacheKey == null) "none" else "set"}, " +
            "jsonSchema=${if (jsonSchema == null) "none" else "set"}, context=${context?.let { "${it.length} chars" } ?: "none"}, " +
            "cacheAfter=${cacheAfter ?: "none"}, cacheFields=$cacheFields)"
}

/**
 * The cache fields that only VS Code's client shows Copilot to pass on (research r51), each of which the agent can switch
 * off for a model whose cache stays empty: Anthropic's `cache_control` on the context and on message `cacheAfter` (and
 * Bedrock's matching cache points), OpenAI's explicit mode with its breakpoints on Copilot's `/responses`, and
 * `copilot_cache_control` on Copilot's `/chat/completions` (design D5 of sub-project 5).
 */
@Serializable
data class CacheFields(val anthropicMarks: Boolean = true, val responsesExplicit: Boolean = true, val chatCopilotMarks: Boolean = true) {
    companion object {
        val ALL = CacheFields()
        val NONE = CacheFields(anthropicMarks = false, responsesExplicit = false, chatCopilotMarks = false)
    }
}

enum class ToolChoice { AUTO, REQUIRED, NONE }
```

Replace the whole `core/providers/src/main/kotlin/dev/kestrel/providers/chat/ChatRequests.kt` with:

```kotlin
package dev.kestrel.providers.chat

/** Checks a request before any adapter runs (design D3). */
object ChatRequests {
    /**
     * Throws IllegalArgumentException when a tool call of an assistant message has no result with its ID before the next
     * user or assistant message, when two calls of one message share an ID, when a tool result's ID belongs to no earlier
     * call (design D32 item 8 of sub-project 5), when `cacheAfter` names no message, or when maxOutputTokens is not
     * positive. Every style refuses a call without a result and a result without its call (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock;
     * Gemini wants all calls of a step before their results).
     */
    fun check(request: ChatRequest) {
        require(request.maxOutputTokens > 0) { "maxOutputTokens must be positive" }
        val messages = request.messages
        request.cacheAfter?.let { require(it in messages.indices) { "cacheAfter names no message" } }
        val called = HashSet<String>()
        for ((index, message) in messages.withIndex()) {
            if (message is ChatMessage.ToolResult) {
                require(message.callId in called) { "Message $index is a tool result without its call" }
                continue
            }
            if (message !is ChatMessage.Assistant) continue
            val calls = message.toolCalls
            if (calls.isEmpty()) continue
            val ids = calls.map { it.id }
            require(ids.toSet().size == ids.size) { "Message $index has two tool calls with one ID" }
            called += ids
            val results = messages.drop(index + 1)
                .takeWhile { it is ChatMessage.ToolResult }
                .map { (it as ChatMessage.ToolResult).callId }
                .toSet()
            val missing = ids.count { it !in results }
            require(missing == 0) { "Message $index has $missing tool calls without a result" }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
    /**
     * Whether an error reply's JSON names the tool choice (design D4 of sub-project 5): OpenAI's `error.param` is
     * `tool_choice`, or the body holds `tool_choice`, `tool choice`, `toolChoice`, `function_calling_config` or
     * `disable_parallel_tool_use` in any case. Only the answer is kept, never the words.
     */
    fun namesToolChoice(reply: HttpReply): Boolean {
        val body = try {
            json.parseToJsonElement(reply.text()) as? JsonObject
        } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {
            null
        } ?: return false
        if ((body["error"] as? JsonObject)?.string("param") == "tool_choice") return true
        val text = body.toString().lowercase()
        return TOOL_CHOICE_WORDS.any { it in text }
    }

    private val TOOL_CHOICE_WORDS = listOf("tool_choice", "tool choice", "toolchoice", "function_calling_config", "disable_parallel_tool_use")

    private fun aws(value: String): String? = value.substringAfter('#').substringBefore(':').trim().takeIf(CODE::matches)
```

```kotlin
    /** The separator line between the system prompt and the per-task context in one system message (design D5 of sub-project 5). */
    const val CONTEXT_SEPARATOR = "\n\n----\n\n"

    /** The system prompt and the request's context as one text, for the styles that keep one system message. */
    fun systemAndContext(request: ChatRequest): String =
        listOf(request.system, request.context.orEmpty()).filter { it.isNotBlank() }.joinToString(CONTEXT_SEPARATOR)

    /**
     * [messages] with each run of adjacent user messages merged into one that holds all their parts, each with the indices
     * of [messages] that it holds, because some local servers' chat templates refuse two user turns in a row (design D5 of
     * sub-project 5).
     */
    fun mergeUsers(messages: List<ChatMessage>): List<Pair<ChatMessage, IntRange>> {
        val merged = mutableListOf<Pair<ChatMessage, IntRange>>()
        for ((index, message) in messages.withIndex()) {
            val last = merged.lastOrNull()
            val previous = last?.first
            if (message is ChatMessage.User && previous is ChatMessage.User) {
                merged[merged.lastIndex] = ChatMessage.User(previous.parts + message.parts) to (last.second.first..index)
            } else {
                merged += message to (index..index)
            }
        }
        return merged
    }

    /** How a tool call goes back as text when the request sends no tools (design D5, research r39). */
```
